---
title: "Attack Efficiency and Winning in LOVB"
subtitle: "An exploratory look at the 2025 season"
format: html
---

## Project question

Does a women's professional volleyball team's attacking performance tend to
move together with its match winning percentage? This page starts to explore
that question using League One Volleyball (LOVB) teams from the 2025 season.

The league's team statistics page reports **Kill Efficiency**, rather than a
measure explicitly named attack percentage. The plot uses Kill Efficiency as
an attack-related measure and keeps the league's label so the two statistics
are not mistaken for one another.

## 2025 team comparison

The table below pairs each team's league-reported Kill Efficiency with its
winning percentage. Winning percentage is calculated as wins divided by total
matches in the published 2025 schedule.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

team_data <- tibble(
  team = c("Atlanta", "Austin", "Houston", "Madison", "Omaha", "Salt Lake"),
  kill_efficiency = c(25.7, 22.1, 22.4, 24.1, 22.3, 23.8),
  wins = c(14, 10, 13, 8, 7, 8),
  losses = c(5, 12, 7, 11, 14, 11)
) |>
  mutate(
    matches = wins + losses,
    win_percentage = wins / matches
  )

team_data |>
  transmute(
    Team = team,
    `Kill efficiency (%)` = kill_efficiency,
    Wins = wins,
    Losses = losses,
    `Win percentage` = scales::percent(win_percentage, accuracy = 0.1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
ggplot(team_data, aes(x = kill_efficiency, y = win_percentage, label = team)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "#7b4ab5", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(color = "#d44a8c", size = 3) +
  geom_text(vjust = -0.8, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Attack efficiency and match wins",
    subtitle = "Each point represents one LOVB team in the 2025 season",
    x = "League-reported kill efficiency",
    y = "Match winning percentage",
    caption = "Sources: LOVB 2025 team statistics and schedule"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Across these six teams, the exploratory Pearson correlation is
`r round(cor(team_data$kill_efficiency, team_data$win_percentage), 2)`.
This small, team-level comparison is descriptive: it does not show that
attacking efficiency causes teams to win.

## Data sources and limitations

- [LOVB 2025 team statistics](https://www.lovb.com/2025/league-statistics) —
  season totals, including the league's Kill Efficiency measure.
- [LOVB 2025 schedule](https://www.lovb.com/2025/schedule) — published match
  results used to count each team's wins and losses.

The teams did not all play the same number of matches, so winning percentage
uses each team's own number of matches. A next step is to confirm whether
match-level attack attempts and errors are available to calculate a
conventional attack percentage directly.
